## Structure and components

- [statement] A custom `Codec` implements `encode()`, `decode()`, and `getEncoderClass()`; the codec registry must contain a codec for the Scala type being encoded or decoded. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/scala/scala-driver/current/data-formats/codecs.md · keywords: Scala driver Observables and case-class codecs

## How it works

- [statement] A `CodecRegistry` is immutable. Compose custom codecs or providers with the default registry, placing custom codecs first when overriding defaults. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/scala/scala-driver/current/data-formats/codecs.md · keywords: Scala driver Observables and case-class codecs

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Scala migration guidance says the Scala 3 compiler cannot expand Scala 2.13 macros. Using `-Xignore-scala2-macros` permits type checking but macro calls throw at runtime; use a library version published for Scala 3. (low confidence) — https://docs.scala-lang.org/scala3/guides/migration/macros.html · keywords: Scala driver Observables and case-class codecs

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The Scala driver builds on the MongoDB Java Reactive Streams driver; its `Observable` extends `Publisher` and adds convenience methods for processing operation results. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/scala/scala-driver/current/crud/query/observables.md · keywords: Scala driver Observables and case-class codecs
- [statement] Calling `subscribe()` with an `Observer` requests operation results; `FindObservable[T]`, `DistinctObservable[T]`, and `AggregateObservable[T]` also support operation-specific configuration before subscription. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/scala/scala-driver/current/crud/query/observables.md · keywords: Scala driver Observables and case-class codecs
- [statement] An `Observer` receives results through `onNext`, terminal failures through `onError`, and completion through `onComplete`; subscription overloads also accept lambda callbacks. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/scala/scala-driver/current/crud/query/observables.md · keywords: Scala driver Observables and case-class codecs · also: http://mongodb.github.io/mongo-scala-driver/2.1/reference/observables/
- [statement] Calling `toFuture()` implicitly subscribes and collects emitted items; for a large document result set this can consume significant memory, so the guide recommends callbacks or lambdas. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/scala/scala-driver/current/crud/query/observables.md · keywords: Scala driver Observables and case-class codecs
- [statement] The historical Scala driver 2.1 contract allows multiple subscriptions to an `Observable`, with each subscription potentially repeating side effects such as queries or inserts. (low confidence) — http://mongodb.github.io/mongo-scala-driver/2.1/reference/observables/ · keywords: Scala driver Observables and case-class codecs
- [statement] The custom case-class example obtains field codecs from a `CodecRegistry` and attaches the composed registry to a typed collection using `withCodecRegistry()`. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/scala/scala-driver/current/data-formats/codecs.md · keywords: Scala driver Observables and case-class codecs
